Actual design pressure of VIP-18 and actual set pressure of PSV-101: If the set pressure is above the design pressure, PSV-101 will not keep the line at or below design and this design fails; the verified 230 psig holding pressure also changes to the actual set pressure.

PSV-101 relieving capacity and that its discharge route is open and goes to a safe location: The simulator assumes the valve can pass whatever is needed; if the real valve or discharge route cannot, pressure can rise above the set pressure during a lift and the 10-day conclusion fails.

Actual heat leak / vacuum condition of VIP-18: If heat leak exceeds the assumed worst 30 W/m, the line becomes liquid-full sooner, the relief load is larger than assumed, and the timing and relief-capacity checks must be redone.

Actual liquid fill when the second block valve is closed: The verified case already uses the top of the assumed range (0.95); if the line could actually be liquid-full at closure, pressure would rise far sooner and the procedure must require draining first.

Whether a calibrated pressure reading and high-pressure alarm exist on the blocked-in segment: Without a pressure reading there is no alarm that can act before PSV-101 lifts; in that case relief restoration alone is not an approved isolation and the alarm plan in this answer cannot be met.

HV-101 actual position and whether its position is indicated/alarmed: If HV-101 is not fully open, PSV-101 is still isolated and the isolated-case timings apply (design passed at 26.2 hours in the worst case), so maintenance must not start.
